title: Refunds of Credit Standing on an Insured Plan of Care
content:
**Insured Plan of Care — refunding a credit.** The refundable credit is the part of the credit standing on a plan of care that is returned to the patient now; whatever is held back stays on the plan as a credit until the reason for holding it ends. The credit standing on the plan is refunded, less what is held back, within the payer program's credit refund period after it arose.

## Basis

The refundable credit is fixed only after every coinsurance charge on the plan that is higher than the share its explanation of benefits supports carries a billing error correction.

The refundable credit is not worked out until each visit on the plan that ran past the payer's visit limit under a signed waiver carries its non-covered service charge.

Read together: while any coinsurance charge on the plan stands above the share its explanation of benefits supports without a billing error correction against it, the refundable credit is not yet fixed; and while any visit that ran past the visit limit under a signed waiver stands without its non-covered service charge, the refundable credit is not yet worked out.

## Issuing the refund — `issue_credit_refund_cc5fc5ad`

**Capability.** One call records a single refund entry dated today against the payment named, by the refund method given, and raises the plan's patient balance by the amount, so the credit owed to the patient shrinks by what is refunded. The patient receives the money back on the original card or by mailed check and can see the refund in the plan history.

**How it is invoked.** An agent-side tool outside the standing tool list: unlock it with `unlock_agent_discoverable_tool`, then call it with `call_agent_discoverable_tool` under the name `issue_credit_refund_cc5fc5ad`.

**Parameters.**

| Parameter | Meaning | Format and values |
|---|---|---|
| `care_plan_id` | The reference number of the insured plan of care the credit stands on, as returned by the plan-of-care lookup | Identifier |
| `source_event_id` | The reference number of the patient payment entry the refund returns, as returned by the plan-of-care history lookup | Identifier |
| `refund_method` | How the money goes back | `original_card` — returned to the card the payment was made with; `check` — mailed to the patient as a paper check |
| `amount` | The amount refunded | USD, a positive number with 2 decimal places, rounded half up to the cent before it is passed |

**Return.** A dictionary confirming the refund: `refund_id` (the reference number of the new refund entry), `care_plan_id`, `source_event_id` (the payment returned), `refund_method` (original_card or check), `amount` (USD to 2 decimals), `event_date` (YYYY-MM-DD, the date issued) and `patient_balance` (USD to 2 decimals, the plan's patient balance after the refund; negative means credit still standing). A returned `refund_id` means the refund has been issued.

**Hypothetical illustration.** A plan with a balance of -60.00 (a $60.00 credit) from which $45.00 is refunded shows a `patient_balance` of -15.00 afterwards: $15.00 of credit stays on the plan.
